subject: Error too many variables in ridge regression

messages.author: 4930488f69589d77
messages.subject: Error too many variables in ridge regression
parts:
All,

I am modeling some binary data using use logistic ridge regression.  I replicated the 3 parameters Stacks example on the INLA site and got reasonable results for my logistic regression for 5 parameters.  However, when I increased the number of parameters/betas to 30, I received the message below.  My questions are: 1) what is the upper limit for ridge regression? and 2) If you do have an upper limit, do you have an alternate recommendation on how to proceed in INLA?  Thanks developing and sharing this statistical software!

Dan Rawding

I am using an older version  of R version 3.3.3 (2017-03-06) -- "Another Canoe"  and INLA’ version 17.06.20. 

Error in INLA::f(beta1, zln_flow, model = "iid", values = c(1, 2, 3, 4,  : 
  To many variables included in f(): beta1 zln_flow

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Error too many variables in ridge regression
parts:
The error can be replicated using more than 2 unnamed arguments, like
this

> inla(y ~ f(i,j,k), data = data.frame(y=0,i=1,j=2,k=3))
Error in INLA::f(i, j, k) : To many variables included in f(): i j k

but the printout from the your error only shows two variables, not 'i j
k' as above.

Anyway, I would guess that model='z' would be easier to use if you want
to do ridge regression, as you can pass all the covariates in a matrix,
like data = list(Z=z); see inla.doc("^z$")

H

messages.author: 4930488f69589d77
messages.subject: Re: Error too many variables in ridge regression
parts:
Harvard,

Thanks for the reply. With your response I figured out my problem.
I was running a model with 5 covariates and 25 interaction terms. The model ran fine for the first five covariates but for the remaining interaction terms I defined them by multiplying combinations of the first 5 covariates as in f(beta6, var1*var2, copy="beta1", fixed=T). Obviously this was wrong so now I defined b6<- var1*var2 and replaced the above expression with f(beta6, b6, copy="beta1", fixed=T).  I did the same for the remaining 24 and the model is working. Thanks for helping me understand this error.

Dan Rawding
